papers.summary:
-  We parsed 37 variable definitions from codebook/README files.
-  12 of 2296 data columns (1%) are documented in a codebook; 2284 are not.
-  A codebook was found and parsed (37 variable definitions), but its variable names do not match the data columns, so the documentation could not be linked automatically (only 1% of columns matched). For example, the codebook documents `Chr`, `*additional columns*`, `Cluster1 / Haplotype1` while the data has `sequencing_id`, `coriell_id`, `kgp_id`. This often means the data holds computed scores or subscales while the codebook lists the underlying items. To make the codebook usable automatically, document variables under the exact names used in the data file (one row per data column), with a label and, for rating items, the response scale.
